from.place: proof step: finite-flat pushforward is finite locally free

title: Finite locally free pushforward along a finite flat morphism
statement: Let $g:X\to Y$ be a finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\mathcal F$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module, i.e. $X$ has an open cover on each member of which $\mathcal F$ is locally free of some constant finite rank [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Then $g_*\mathcal F$ is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_Y$-module in the same sense.

proof.text: Because a finite morphism is affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], the inverse image of every affine open of $Y$ is affine. This supplies the affine morphism hypothesis needed below.

The finite locally free hypothesis on $\mathcal F$ gives local freeness and quasi-coherence by [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Applying the affine pushforward quasi-coherence statement [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change] to $g$ and $\mathcal F$ shows that $g_*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent.

Let $V\subseteq Y$ be affine and put $V'=g^{-1}(V)$. By Step 1, $V'$ is affine. The sections $M=\Gamma(V',\mathcal F)$ are finitely presented and projective over $B=\Gamma(V',\mathcal O_X)$ by [lem-pc-finite-flat-affine-sections-projective]. Put $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Y)$. Since $g$ is finite, $B$ is a finite $A$-module by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; since $g$ is locally of finite presentation and $g(V')\subseteq V$ with $V,V'$ affine, $A\to B$ is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]; since $g$ is flat, $B$ is a flat $A$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. Hence [lem-pc-finite-flat-restriction-projective] makes $M$ finitely presented and projective as an $A$-module; projective modules are flat, and the $A$-module of sections of $g_*\mathcal F$ on $V$ is exactly $M$ by the definition of direct image.

The affine criterion [lem-pc-affine-sections-finite-locally-free-criterion], applied to the quasi-coherent sheaf from Step 2 and the finitely presented flat section module from Step 3 on every affine open $V$, yields that $g_*\mathcal F$ is finite locally free over $\mathcal O_Y$.
